title: Kies de visuele wereld voor Sanitair Verschraegen
question: The roll assigned Bestelwagen-belettering (trade van livery). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Bestelwagen-belettering
options.lineage: Flemish installer vans and magnetic site signs: blue panels, white condensed caps, a phone number you can read at 50 km/h
options.thesis: The site is the company van: who, what and the phone number, readable at a glance, then their real work.
materials: white vinyl lettering in heavy condensed caps
the grey service block from their logo
real site photos as windows in the panel
options.viewport: Full-width brand-blue panel: huge VM monogram + VERSCHRAEGEN, the grey block naming the four trades, a big tap-to-call number and 'Offerte aanvragen'; a real bathroom photo cut into the panel like a van window.
options.risk: Can tip into flat corporate-blue if the lettering scale and photo crops are timid.

raised.raise: Restricted ink set: blue, grey, white and the photos. Nothing else enters the page, not even a hover colour.
Realisaties you mark ('Dit wil ik ook') travel into the offerte form, persisted locally.
One condensed grotesk throughout; rank by panel size, not by more fonts. Narrow screens drop columns, never type size.
One reserved active signal (white panel inversion) used only for the current state.

options.label: Tegelraster
options.lineage: the tiled bathroom wall: 30x60 tiles, grout lines, the tiler's layout
options.thesis: The page is a tiled wall: grout lines are the grid, every photo and fact sits on whole tiles.
options.viewport: A wall of tiles where some tiles are photos, one tile carries the logo, and the phone number fills a tile row.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a bathroom firm; risks reading as a tile-shop template.

options.label: Cutting bench select rail
options.lineage: film editor's work print on pins
options.thesis: Projects strung as frames along a scrubbing rail.
options.viewport: A perforated rail of project frames across an orange field.
options.risk: Homeowners do not identify with film editing.
options.case: Fuses: realisaties become frames on a rail, but clients don't recognise it and orange fights the brand.
options.kept: One condensed grotesk, rank by size of panel.

options.label: Convention circle catalog
options.lineage: newsprint thumbnail catalog circled in biro
options.thesis: All projects as a dense grid you circle.
options.viewport: Hundreds of tiny project thumbnails, a few circled.
options.risk: Low-res photos look worse dense; newsprint cheapens the trade.
options.case: Fuses: realisaties as a circle-able grid; loses on audience and clarity.
options.kept: Mark projects you like and carry them into the quote.

options.label: Socialist kiosk print
options.thesis: Services as goods in a restricted-ink kiosk grid.
options.viewport: A grid of service 'products' in three inks, no photos.
options.risk: No photos would throw away their strongest proof.
options.case: Fuses: services as kiosk cells; but bans the photos that sell the work.

options.label: Hand-processed film bloom
options.thesis: Project photos as damaged film frames.
options.viewport: A scratched film strip of bathrooms.
options.risk: Damage aesthetics contradict a firm selling clean, finished work.
options.case: Fuses poorly: wear and damage say the opposite of quality installation.
options.kept: One reserved signal for the active state.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.thesis: Sections as blocks cut from clouds.
options.viewport: A cumulus cliff with blue voids.
options.risk: Surreal and vague; homeowners want concrete reassurance.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dreamlike where the visitor needs facts.
options.kept: Stacked blocks with deep gaps between sections.

options.label: HyperCard stack
options.thesis: Every service and project as a linked card.
options.viewport: A black-and-white card with painted buttons.
options.risk: Nostalgic novelty; no fit with installers.
options.kept: Every project addressable by its own link.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Installer website: full-width bathroom photo hero, three service cards, gallery grid, contact form.
canonCard.viewport: Large bathroom photo with headline overlay and a quote button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other installer; their small photos struggle as full-bleed hero.
